Facts leading to issuance of this Rule may be summarised which are as follows: The First and Second Opposite Parties as plaintiffs instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 32 of 1980 in the Third Court of Subordinate Judge at Comilla for declaration of title and recovery of possession of the suit land. The suit on transfer to the court of the Subordinate Judge, Chandpur was re-numbered as Title Suit No. 172 of 1981. Case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that Chandra Mohan Chowdhury was the owner of the suit land comprising of an area of 0.01 acre of land situated at Mohamaya Bazar. Chandra Mohan Chowdhury settled the same with structures standing thereon in favour of Abdul Jalil Mizi, defendant No. 8 who executed and registered a kabuliyat dated 23-8-1951 on his behalf as well as his full-brother Abdul Jabbar Mizi, the predecessor of defendant Nos.  1 and 2 Abdul Jalil Mizi, acquired the suit land out of the joint family fund for his own benefits and also for the benefit of his full-brother Abdul Jabbar. On amicable partition Abdul Jabbar Mizi used to own and possess northern half of the suit land with the structure described in schedule 1(ka) to the plaint and Abdul Jalil Mizi, used to own and possess the remaining southern portion of the land with the structure described in schedule 1(kah) to the plaint. During Revisional Settlement Operation the suit land was recorded both in the names of Abdul Jalil Mizi and Abdul Jabbar Mizi in Revisional Settlement Khatian No. 134 in equal shares. Abdul Jabbar Mizi transferred his portion of land with structure standing thereon to Serajul Islam Mizi, the defendant No. 9 by registered sale deed dated 16-9-1970 and possession was handed over to the transferee Serajul Islam Mizi. During the War of Liberation Abdul Jabbar Mizi died leaving behind two sons defendant Nos.   1 and 2 who approached their cousin defendant No. 9 in the year 1972 to permit them to start tea stall in ''Ka'' schedule land and permission was accordingly accorded by the defendant No. 9 and the defendant Nos.   1 and 2 since then remained there as licensees under defendant No. 9. Abdul Jalil Mizi also transferred his portion of land with structures thereon in favour of defendant No. 9 by a registered deed of conveyance dated 1-2-1977 and parted with possession. Defendant No. 9 allowed his uncle defendant No. 4 to run a business in the southern half of schedule ''Ka'' land as a licensee. The defendant Nos.   5 and 6 are the sons of defendant No. 4. The defendant No. 9 being the absolute owner over the suit land and the structures standing thereon, transferred the same in favour of the plaintiffs by way of two registered sale deeds dated 23-6-1979. The plaintiff, after purchase asked the defendant Nos.1-6 to hand over the vacant possession of the suit property in his favour. The defendants got no right, title and interest in the suit land. They having declined to give vacant possession of the suit property, the plaintiffs have been constrained to institute the suit for the reliefs stated above. 

 36. Exhibit-3 is the Deed of Conveyance dated 16-9-1970 executed by Abdul Jabbar Mizi in favour of Md. Serajul Islam the defendant No. 9. In the said deed the schedule 1(ka) property is stated as ChandinaBhiti land and the house standing thereon and the same is also stated to be situated at Mohamaya Bazar. Exhibit-C is the agreement of re-conveyance dated 16-9-70 executed by Serajul Islam in favour of Abdul Jabbar Mizi. In the said agreement of reconveyance also the schedule-1(ka) property has been described as Chandina Bhiti and is stated to be situated at Mohamaya Bazar. Exhibit-8(a) is the certified copy of the Record of Right of the relevant khatian No. 134 wherein the tenancy is stated to be a Non-agricultural tenancy right (সেকস্তি প্রজা স্বত্ব) and the schedule-1(ka) property has been stated to be shop (দোকান).
